mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which increases discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the 5th percentile of the historical distribution at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent surge in the Consumer Price Index above 4% signals a stagflation risk, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the 10th percentile of the historical distribution at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the previous six-month average while personal income growth (PAYEMS) stagnates signals a shift from spending to saving, which depresses consumption-driven sectors and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 6-month moving average AND PAYEMS monthly change < 0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate below 4% for six consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which typically precedes restrictive policy responses and profit margin compression, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous 12-month average during a period of stable inflation signals improving residential investment and broader demand recovery, which boosts construction and related sectors and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average AND CPIAUCSL monthly change within ±0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).
